newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EVERTON CHASING SWISS INTERNATIONAL SFORZA:.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVERTON CHASING SWISS INTERNATIONAL SFORZA:.

text.p: Everton are close to signing Internazionale's Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza, the English club's manager Howard Kendall said on Monday.
"We are very near to agreeing a deal," Kendall told Everton's official clubcall service.

The newly-appointed manager, who presided over the Liverpool club's glory years in the mid-1980s when they won the league twice and the European Cup Winners' Cup, said Everton had been in contact with the Milan club.
Kendall hoped that the talks would lead to the player making a personal visit this week.
"I'll be delighted if this player comes over and we can sit down. I can sell the football side to him," he said.
The manager described Sforza, who has earned more than 40 caps for his country and who played in the 1994 World Cup, as "an outstanding player...a leader".

The Sunday People newspaper reported at the weekend that Everton had offered 3 million pounds ($5 million) for Sforza, outbidding his former German Bundesliga club Kaiserslautern who sold him on to Bayern Munich in 1995.
The paper said Kaiserslautern had been due to sign Sforza at the weekend but Inter had stopped the talks and the player had asked for the weekend to make up his mind.
The player's agent Martin Wizner was quoted by the newspaper as saying: "We have two offers to consider and Ciri will give his answer in the next few days."
If Sforza does decide to move to Everton, he will find himself in the same city as his former Inter team mate Paul Ince who has joined local rivals Liverpool.
He will also be the latest player lured from serie A to English soccer in a busy week of transfers.
Ince signed last week and Juventus winger Attilio Lombardo is expected to finalise a transfer to newly-promoted Crystal Palace shortly.
Lombardo, 31, is due in London this week for a medical and to discuss personal terms.
However Palace assistant manager Ray Lewington said on Monday that he had known nothing of the deal until it was announced and warned that Lombardo was a gamble.
He told the Palace clubline that while some Italians had been successful in English soccer, others had not. "If he comes for a big payday, it could backfire on us."
Fiorentina striker Francesco Baiano is also tipped to join Derby County, alongside ex-Milan player Stefano Eranio.

Sforza had been closely linked in his career to former Swiss team and Inter manager Roy Hodgson, now at Blackburn, who made him his first signing at Inter after taking over as coach during the 1995-96 season.
"That speaks volumes for the player and what Roy thinks of him," said Kendall.

The manager added that Everton would be interested in Newcastle striker Les Ferdinand if he became available but were not signing Hungarian international goalkeeper Szabolcs Safar who has been on a week's trial from Vasas Budapest.
Safar played in Everton's 3-0 pre-season friendly defeat by Tranmere Rovers on Saturday.
Kendall said Everton were impressed by Safar but "I'm not progressing with it. He'll be returning to Hungary...I thought we should have a look at him and now we've done that."
Newspapers at the weekend linked Everton with Ferdinand after the England striker appeared to cast doubts on his future as Alan Shearer's strike partner at the club.

Kendall said the media speculation was inevitable after talks to recruit Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli from relegated Middlesbrough hit the rocks last week over wage demands but there had been no contacts.
"We are looking for a quality striker and Ferdinand certainly is that. Should he become available, we'd be interested. But that is not the case at the moment." REUTER 211252 GMT jul 97
